description: Converts geometry between Tekla Structures 2025 and GeometryHelper: points, vectors, segments, planes, coordinate systems, bounding boxes, transformation matrices, and the faces and loops of a Tekla solid. Also reads the objects of IFC reference models into solids placed where Tekla shows them, through GeometryHelper.IfcConvert. Built for Tekla Structures 2025; install the package whose year matches your Tekla.
releaseNotes:
Converts geometry between Tekla Structures and GeometryHelper, both ways: points, vectors, line
      segments, geometric planes, coordinate systems, bounding boxes, transformation matrices, and the
      faces and loops of a Tekla solid.

      BUILT FOR TEKLA STRUCTURES 2025
      - This package references the Tekla Structures 2025 Open API. Tekla's assemblies are
        strong-named per release and a plugin cannot redirect between them, so install the package whose
        year matches your Tekla: GeometryHelper.TeklaConvert.2020, GeometryHelper.TeklaConvert.2025 or
        GeometryHelper.TeklaConvert.2026. It replaces the former GeometryHelper.TeklaConvert package, which
        was built against 2020 only.

      REQUIRES THREE ASSEMBLIES YOU MUST SUPPLY
      - Tekla.Structures.dll, Tekla.Structures.Drawing.dll and Tekla.Structures.Model.dll are not
        redistributed here, because they are Trimble's to ship rather than ours. Reference them yourself,
        either from the bin folder of your Tekla Structures installation or from Trimble's own
        Tekla.Structures, Tekla.Structures.Drawing and Tekla.Structures.Model packages on nuget.org.
        Without them the compiler reports CS0012.

      IFC REFERENCE MODELS
      - ReferenceModelObjectConvert.ToGeoSolids / ToIfcGeometries read the selected objects of IFC
        reference models, and ReferenceModelConvert.ToGeoSolids / ToIfcGeometries every physical product
        of a reference model, in the current work plane: the IFC file is read in millimetres at the
        reference model's scale and placed where the reference model was inserted.
      - ToIfcGeometries returns each IFC product whole (IfcProductGeometry): bodies, open surfaces,
        placement, GlobalId, name, type and conversion warnings.
      - Bolts make a whole Tekla model slow to read. IfcConvertOptions.SkipNames and OnlyNames choose the
        products by name before any geometry is built: a 115 MB steel model read in 35 s without its bolts
        and in 3.5 s for its main members, against about 17 minutes for every product.
      - Reference models that are not IFC, files that cannot be read and objects that cannot be converted
        are left out rather than thrown on, and written to GeometryHelperLog (GeometryHelper).
        Each IFC file is parsed once per process and then cached.
      - These read IFC through GeometryHelper.IfcConvert, which this package depends on. They run on
        .NET Framework 4.8 x64, and Xbim.Geometry.Engine64.dll, which the build copies next to your
        plugin, has to ship with it.

      DRAWING IN THE MODEL VIEW
      - GeometryDraw.DrawToTekla draws polylines, polygons, faces and solids (and DrawPolyline points) as
        control polycurves in the current work plane. Faces are drawn with their outer boundary in red and
        their holes in white unless other colours are passed. An arc or a circle draws as well, cut into
        straight pieces within 0.2 % of its radius, which is finer than a model view resolves. The polycurves are returned so that Delete()
        can take them away again. Call Model.CommitChanges() afterwards; the methods do not commit.

      READING A SOLID
      - Faces are turned to agree with the normal Tekla gives them, and the body is turned inside out
        if its signed volume says the whole surface arrived reversed. A coordinate system whose Y axis
        is not quite square to its X axis is squared up rather than trusted.
      - A face that cannot be made sense of is skipped rather than thrown on, which leaves the body no
        longer closed, so ask IsClosed() before trusting a volume.
      - Tekla models in millimetres with coordinates running to hundreds of thousands, where the
        default EqualPlanar is often too tight. Pass a Tolerance suited to the model.
